candidates.label: Floyd-Warshall once on the full original graph for all-pairs shortest paths (destroyed towers do NOT get excluded as future intermediate nodes -- only removed from the summed pairs), then maintain a running sum over active-tower ordered pairs, subtracting a tower's contribution when it's destroyed, accumulating each step's running sum into a grand total (the actual required output per the worked example: 89+7+0=96, not per-step values). Hand-verified exactly against test cases 1 and 2 of the given sample by tracing Floyd-Warshall and the running-sum bookkeeping by hand.

Identical logic but distances/totals stored as 32-bit int -- with n up to 500 and edge weights up to 1e4, the grand total can reach roughly 500 * 500^2 * 1e4 which overflows int32 by orders of magnitude, but the tiny 3-node sample stays well within int32 so this passes the given sample fine.

Forgets to set active[x]=false after destroying a tower, so every previously-destroyed tower keeps contributing to every later step's sum instead of being excluded -- inflates the grand total on any test case with more than 1 destruction step (case 1 already has 3 steps, so this should diverge on the given sample itself).
